To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) source-specific models are better than a single global model for all sources; (2) similarity score normalization based either on document-specific or on source-pair-specific average similarity score improves the performance of the system significantly; (3) the use of inverse event frequencies improves the performance of our system; and (4) segmentation does not improve the performance of our method.

(1) source-specific models are better than a single, global model; (2) normalization based on document averages is better than no normalization; and (3) normalization based on source-specific averages is better than normalization based on document-averages.

(i) source-specific TF-IDF models outperform a global TF-IDF model, (ii) similarity score normalization based either on source-pair or document-specific averages is beneficial, (iii) segmentation improves the performance, (iv) term reweighting improves performance on the TDT4 data, and (v) the combination of source-specific TF-IDFs, segmentation and normalization is the best performing method.

the development of a robust and accurate system for new event detection, which is able to handle a wide variety of input data and to perform well on a wide variety of test data.
